chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Touring the mining camps from Morenci and Clifton
summary: Shows toured about twenty mining towns using company scrip, with Hattie McDaniel's group joining them, before they went strictly vaudeville.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Oh, about a year, I guess. About six months or a year. That's when we took out our show again. See? We took

out a show out of Morenci. The first show we took out of Prescott. We was playing in Prescott when we took our first show, went 'round, got down as far as Bisbee, then we broke up. Then the next show we took out of uh, Morenc...uh, Presc...uh, uh, I mean Moren...Clifton, and then we went around a trip and bought the two. We only didn't stay just in Arizona. We play maybe twenty little towns and goldmine stations where they had...all the money was company money. You didn't see no American money. Everything was stamped "Golden Western Company" ..."The Great Western Company." Those was the mines, and they had their own money.
Yeah. Everything you spent was like...uh... they pay you off in their own money but it just is the same value as the government money.
So you and your brothers got paid in company money?

No, not we. I'm talking about the miners. The miners. And the next one we took out was from Douglas, you know, and that's when we had Hattie McDaniels and her brother and all of them with us. And after that, we went strictly vaudeville. My older brother, he went back to his barbering and inventions and things. My other brother, Johnny, and I, we travelled with our musical act.
